findings.note: The sole evidence file for the required `requirement-traceability` check is three remediation passes stale and self-dated as such: its header reads "re-verified 2026-08-23 (second pass, AC-056 remediation) at HEAD febf7898", and it was NOT re-captured by the Fifth Pass, which explicitly re-captured regression.log and placeholder-scan.log for exactly this staleness class (contract comment, FIFTH PASS ADDENDUM). Its content contradicts the current tree on facts verifiable from inside this bundle: it records the human-copy MANIFEST entry for resolve-project-context.py as `ca3c95f6...`, while the MANIFEST.sha256 section of this same bundle carries `f6bc679612fff4b0d35f1770fe1f135339090392ba042ef31ad229426316fbd9` (three subsequent supersessions: 783b7f11 -> cb9f050b -> f6bc6796); and its "Implemented ... 141 passed / 0 failed" enumeration describes a four-invocation T-004 fixture set, whereas the reviewed driver runs eight T-004 invocations plus the draft7 validator/coverage meta-assertions at 184/0. The requirement->implementing-test mapping for the code actually under review (the Fifth Pass's `_governing_schema_version_ok`, the safe-exception-text change, `recheck-dependency-failed`, `draft7-keyword-coverage`) is therefore not established by the cited evidence. Remedy: re-run/re-capture traceability.log against current HEAD, as was already done for the two sibling logs.

Step 12's non-Evidence sub-case (AC-055(b)) is exercised only through the Context Projection. The track-exclusive branch -- `track_artifact` (facet-manifest on full, capability-summary on lite) failing `_draft7_conforms` and producing `the staged facet-manifest/capability-summary artifact failed ...` -- has no fixture in this task's suite, so that raise site and detail string are never observed. AC-055's own "**two** independently-triggerable fixtures" wording is satisfied, so non-blocking, but the branch is untested.

Every fixture uses plain component ids (`comp-a`, `comp-z`), so the RFC-6901 `~`->`~0` / `/`->`~1` escaping in `context_binding.dependency_pointers[]` is never exercised. The test oracle is a hand-duplicated copy of the production escape rather than an independent derivation, so a shared error in the escape rule would pass both sides silently. Context Projection `components` constrains keys only with `propertyNames: {minLength: 1}`, so an id containing `/` or `~` is schema-legal input.

`re.search(schema["pattern"], instance)` uses Python regex semantics, in which `$` also matches immediately before a trailing newline. Anchored governing-schema patterns such as `sha256Digest`'s `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` and `feature`'s `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` therefore accept a value with a trailing `\n` that ECMA-262-semantics JSON Schema rejects, making step 12's defensive self-check marginally weaker than the schema it defends. Not reachable from this feature's own generated values (hexdigests carry no newline; `--feature` is guarded by `FEATURE_RE.fullmatch`), hence Minor.
